subject.title: [Bug]: Cron agent jobs silently time out during sustained LLM API outages instead of fast-failing on definitive errors

question: How should plain provider `api_error: Internal server error` failures from cron model runs be classified: cron-local transient, `server_error`, `overloaded`, or left as `timeout`?
rationale: Each option changes retry matching, fast-fail semantics, and whether shared auth-profile cooldown is affected; current code intentionally treats `server_error` as not poisoning auth-profile health while timeout can become profile cooldown after provider start.

options.title: Use cron-local transient
options.body: Treat the plain provider 500 as retryable and fast-failable for cron/fallback without marking shared auth profiles unhealthy unless a separate policy opts in.

options.title: Map to server_error
options.body: Reuse the existing structured `server_error` path so cron state and retry policy report server errors consistently while avoiding shared auth-profile cooldown.

options.title: Map to overloaded
options.body: Use overload cooldown to skip same-provider profiles sooner, accepting the risk that broad HTTP 500 outages affect shared provider health state.

recommendation.title: Use cron-local transient
recommendation.body: Treat the plain provider 500 as retryable and fast-failable for cron/fallback without marking shared auth profiles unhealthy unless a separate policy opts in.

likelyOwner.reason: altaywtf has the strongest available history on nearby internal-500 failover classification and was brought into the issue after the classification-policy split was raised.
